clue.text: Commonly, chap had a mass of hair slicked back with this

definitions.text: Commonly, chap had a mass of hair slicked back with this

indicators.note: hair slicked back is swept the wrong way, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: he'd, said commonly with the H dropped, is 'ed: chap is he, and he'd is he had
a mop is a thick mass of hair

explanation.surface: A dropped-aitch description of a man greasing back his thick hair with some product.
explanation.walkthrough: Commonly drops the H, so 'chap had' (he'd) becomes 'ED. Add A and MOP, then read EDAMOP backwards. The whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomade is a scented hair grease used to slick hair down and back.

clue.text: Shakespeare's mistress and attendant

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Mistress ..., one of The Merry Wives of Windsor
second meaning: a boy servant or messenger

explanation.walkthrough: Mistress here is a title, as in Mistress Page of The Merry Wives of Windsor, not a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A page is a young servant who waits on a noble, and Mistress Page is a Shakespeare character.

clue.text: Perhaps a place in hotel raised charge to stay

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, signals perhaps
a room is a place to sleep in a hotel

explanation.surface: A guest is charged extra to keep a hotel room.
explanation.walkthrough: EG A ROOM, read upwards as this is a down clue, gives the answer; the hotel picture hides a boating sense of stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorage is the fee paid for keeping a boat tied up at a mooring.

clue.text: Departs one precise area

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
I is the Roman numeral for one
strict means exact or precise

explanation.surface: A train leaves at an exact time for a particular area.
explanation.definitionFit: A district is a region or locality, so it is a synonym for area.

clue.text: About to make a mistake, wearing sensible white

indicators.note: the outer word is wearing the others, so they go inside it

parts.note: sane means sensible
C is short for circa, about
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone about to slip up while dressed in sensible white clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White' looks like clothing in the surface but is the definition: a white wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sancerre is a white wine from the Loire valley in France.

clue.text: Different tea interval organised

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tea break arranged in an unusual way.
explanation.definitionFit: An alternative option is another, different one from the usual.

clue.text: Pass our flag

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: An instruction to hand over our flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour, usually in the plural, is a regimental or national banner.

clue.text: Retired person returning has to go over the same ground

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who has retired and been brought back to work

definitions.text: to go over the same ground
definitions.meaning: second meaning: to tread a path again

explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' looks like a reversal signal, but it belongs to the first meaning: a retired person returning to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Retread as a noun is slang for a re-employed retiree, and as a verb means to walk the same route again.

clue.text: Duty officer

parts.note: reads as the officer on duty, but means an official who collects excise duty

explanation.walkthrough: Duty here is a tax, not a shift at work.
explanation.definitionFit: An exciseman was a government official who collected excise taxes on goods.

clue.text: This to eat gives one bellyache

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a game bird that is eaten

explanation.walkthrough: Bellyache is slang for grumble, not a stomach upset after eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouse is a game bird cooked and eaten, and to grouse is to complain.

clue.text: Vigorous, I shake the talc around

indicators.note: shake means jumble up, so these letters are rearranged
around supports the shake, moving the letters about

explanation.definitionFit: Athletic means physically strong and energetic, close to vigorous.

clue.text: Garment that only half suits one

definitions.text: Garment that only half suits one

parts.words: Garment that only half suits one
parts.note: a two-piece suit is jacket and trousers, so this garment is half of a suit

explanation.walkthrough: 'Suits' looks like a verb meaning flatters, but it is the noun: one garment of a two-piece suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousers are a single garment counted as a pair, and with a jacket they make up a suit.

clue.text: A field of runners is so energetic

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a field planted with runner beans is literally packed with beans
second meaning: lively and full of energy

explanation.walkthrough: Runners sound like athletes, but runner beans are a common British climbing bean.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of beans is an idiom for lively and high-spirited.

clue.text: It's clear rebel got drunk down here

definitions.text: It's clear rebel got drunk down here

indicators.note: drunk suggests something messed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An obvious spot where a rebel got drunk below ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer as well: a place downstairs where one gets drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A beer cellar is an underground room for storing or drinking beer.

clue.text: One played with infant: kind of mother!

parts.note: a baby is an infant
grand, as in grandmother

explanation.surface: A mother playing with her baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One played' means an instrument: a small grand piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby grand is a small grand piano, an instrument that is played.

clue.text: One coming from Holland forced to return

indicators.note: to return means turning back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: made, as in made to do something, means forced

explanation.surface: A Dutch person compelled to go back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One coming from Holland' looks like a Dutch person but is the cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a round Dutch cheese named after a town in Holland.

clue.text: Supports suggestion not to finish bottom

parts.note: backs means supports

indicators.note: not finishing means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an idea is a suggestion

explanation.surface: Someone backs a suggestion for not finishing at the bottom of a table.
explanation.definitionFit: Backside is an informal word for buttocks, the bottom.

clue.text: Using head, attack bum

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to strike with the head

explanation.walkthrough: Bum is the British slang for buttocks, not the American tramp.
explanation.definitionFit: To butt is to ram with the head, and a butt is slang for buttocks.

clue.text: Title character misspelled in our list

indicators.note: a word misspelled has its letters in the wrong order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A name in a title was spelt wrong in our list.
explanation.definitionFit: Troilus is the hero named in the title of Shakespeare's Troilus and Cressida.

clue.text: The whole country after one day backing candidate

indicators.note: the country comes after the other letters
backing means going backwards, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Mon is the abbreviation for Monday
a nation is a whole country

explanation.surface: A whole nation rallies behind a candidate one day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like a country supporting its candidate, but it is the reversal signal; 'after' puts the country last.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomination is a person put forward for election, so a candidate.

clue.text: Sort of rock, belting out half-ugly noise

indicators.note: belting out suggests a loud, rough performance, so the letters are jumbled
half of the word ugly is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A rock singer belting out a half-ugly noise.
explanation.walkthrough: UG, the first half of 'ugly', is mixed with the letters of NOISE. 'Rock' is the stone, not the music.
explanation.definitionFit: Igneous rock forms when molten magma cools and sets solid, like granite or basalt.

clue.text: Rod left in rage

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the other word

parts.note: anger is rage

explanation.surface: Someone named Rod storms off in a fury.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod looks like a name or a fishing rod, but it stands for the person holding one.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler fishes with a rod, so a rod here names the person who holds it.

clue.text: Innovative way to make dog run?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to build a dog run, an outdoor enclosure, you would first be breaking ground

explanation.walkthrough: A dog run is a fenced pen; 'make' is construct, not force a dog to run.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground-breaking work is pioneering and new, like breaking fresh earth.

clue.text: As dye plant, use some vanilla

indicators.note: use some means only some of the letters of the next word are taken, which conceals the answer

explanation.surface: A cook is told to treat some vanilla as if it were a dye plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is the indigo shrub, a plant whose leaves produce a blue dye.

clue.text: No danger of fog, it's understood

definitions.meaning: first meaning: everything is clear, with no fog anywhere
second meaning: the matter is completely clear

explanation.walkthrough: The all-clear is the signal that danger has passed; here the setter reads it literally as clear skies.
explanation.definitionFit: All clear signals safety, and read literally says the weather is clear and the meaning plain.

clue.text: Have nothing to do with row about pig

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the noise goes around the pig

parts.note: din is a noisy row
a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: Someone avoids a quarrel over a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown is to refuse to acknowledge or be associated with someone.

clue.text: Died, I make quite clear, in great suffering

parts.note: d is the genealogy abbreviation for died
to stress a point is to make it quite clear

explanation.surface: A last statement emphasising a painful death.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is severe anxiety, pain or anguish.

clue.text: Sly creature in pop song?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small cunning mammal
second meaning: the animal in the nursery rhyme Pop Goes the ...

explanation.walkthrough: Pop song suggests the charts, but it is the old rhyme Pop Goes the Weasel.
explanation.definitionFit: The weasel is a small predator proverbial for slyness, and stars in the old rhyme.
